title: Admin access intake classification -> resolution lifecycle
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers routinely request admin and access changes (RBAC updates, SSO/SAML integrations, SCIM provisioning, org policies). Current intake is ad-hoc: tickets arrive via Support, sales, and emailed spreadsheets. This creates slow decision cycles, inconsistent priority handling, and occasional security/SCIM misconfigurations. Goal: define a deterministic classification and routing lifecycle that converts every admin/access request into a triaged package: classification (risk + scope), SLA + routing (who owns initial work), and resolution pattern (self-serve, config change, engineering change, or security review). This ticket captures the PM definition, acceptance criteria, decision heuristics, and an implementation-ready handoff to Eng & Security for an automated intake form + routing rules.
acceptance_criteria: Published classification rubric that assigns a numeric risk score (1-10) based on customer tier, data sensitivity, action surface area, and need-for-code

Defined routing map: which requests go to Support Ops (self-serve doc + step-through), which to Identity team (SSO/SCIM), which to Platform Engineering (RBAC platform changes), and which to Security for manual review
An intake form prototype (Confluence + short form) with required fields, example values, and validation rules
Automation spec describing webhook triggers to create correct Linear ticket prefix and populate labels + SLA timers
KPI dashboard defined: mean time to triage, percent auto-routed, mean time to resolution by route, and escaped changes requiring rollback
Stakeholder approval from Security, Identity, Support, and Sales engineering documented in comments
work_notes: 2026-02-26: Kickoff with Security, Identity, Support Ops. Initial pain points captured: unclear data classification, no consistent SCIM schema mapping, and ad-hoc SSO cert exchange process.

2026-03-02: Drafted initial risk rubric. Proposal: risk_score = customer_tier_weight (1-4) + data_sensitivity (0-3) + blast_radius (0-2) + implementation_complexity (0-1). Discussed pros/cons with Security (they prefer finer granularity for data sensitivity).

2026-03-05: Prototype intake form fields enumerated. Required: customer_org_id, requester_email, action_type (RBAC|SSO|SCIM|OrgPolicy), current_impact, desired_outcome, example_users/roles affected, evidence (screenshots/configs), urgency_reason, compliance_tags (e.g., HIPAA, SOC2), customer_tier.

2026-03-09: Trade-offs: aggressive automation reduces latency but increases risk of misapplied RBAC changes. Decided to auto-route but gate high-risk (>7) actions behind a manual Security approval step.

2026-03-11: Handoff to Eng: create webhook mapping that converts form submissions into Linear tickets with key prefix PM- or ENG- depending on route. Also request a small orchestration microservice to enforce SLA timers and escalate when approver doesn't act within SLA.

2026-03-12: Prepared implementation spec for Console UI addendum (in-console admin request CTA) and in-product links to self-serve docs. Requested estimate from ENG-4129 for routing microservice and from Identity for SCIM schema templates.
comments: Liam O'Connor (Security) 2026-03-01: Reviewed risk rubric draft. Suggest splitting data_sensitivity into PII vs. regulated data. Also propose mandatory compliance_tags for any request from enterprise customers.
Riley Cheng 2026-03-03: Adding a 'sandboxable' flag to intake so we can offer customers a test rollout path instead of immediate prod changes — reduces incident risk.

Maya Singh (Support Ops) 2026-03-06: From Support perspective, we need templated response fragments and an instrumented checklist to reduce back-and-forth. Will own self-serve doc updates once routing is live.

Victor Alvarez (Identity) 2026-03-08: SCIM requests frequently fail due to schema mapping. Propose we include an optional JSON attachment and a 'mapping_help' field that links to our mapping guide. Also recommend automating a pre-validation step against customer's SCIM endpoint when possible.

Asha Patel 2026-03-10: Decision: auto-route low-risk RBAC and documentation requests to Support Ops with SLA 3 business days; medium-risk SSO/SCIM to Identity with SLA 5 business days; high-risk or compliance-tagged to Security with 2 business-day manual review. Recorded in acceptance criteria.

Riley Cheng 2026-03-12: Submitted draft webhook mapping to ENG-4129 for review: mapping table includes action_type->team, risk_score->label, compliance_tags->labels, customer_tier->priority override. ENG to add SLA timer fields and escalate endpoints.
next_steps: Priority 1: Eng (ENG-4129) to build webhook endpoint and ticket-mapping logic (estimate requested)
Priority 2: Identity to produce SCIM mapping templates and a validation script to attach to intake form
Priority 3: Support Ops to author self-serve flows for low-risk RBAC and policy FAQs
Priority 4: Security to finalize manual review checklist and SLA for high-risk items
Priority 5: PM to coordinate console CTA placement and run a 2-week pilot with 3 enterprise customers
